text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and U.S. President Bill Clinton to hold summit meeting today and talk about pushing forward the peace process and bilateral ties. The president will focus on resuming peace talks on all tracks and ceasing settlements in Israel.
- The president tells Cable News Network (CNN): Settlements create serious problems and Washington can help out the peace process.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says cabinet will discuss rain drainage system for Cairo this year.
- Mubarak will spend four hours in the White House today.
- Governorate to divide Cairo into four sectors to begin work on the rains drainage system.
- International Monetary Fund officials say that Egypt has achieved visible economic growth.
- Religious Endowments Minister Mahmoud Hamdi Zakzouk says cloning of human beings is totally unacceptable.
